items.question: Pulling your hand back from a flame before you have thought about it is an example of what?
items.explanation: The response is quick and happens without conscious thought, which is what we mean by a reflex.

items.question: In which order does an electrical impulse travel through a neuron?
options: Axon, then cell body, then dendrite
Dendrite, then cell body, then along the axon
Cell body, then dendrite, then axon
items.explanation: Information picked up at the dendrite tip becomes an impulse that passes to the cell body and then down the axon.

items.question: How do the shoots of a plant respond to light?
options: They do not respond at all
items.explanation: Shoots show positive phototropism and grow towards light; roots bend away from it.

items.question: Which hormone helps regulate the level of sugar in the blood?
items.explanation: Insulin, made by the pancreas, controls blood sugar; without enough of it the sugar level rises.

items.question: Which part of the brain keeps the posture and balance of the body?
items.explanation: The cerebellum in the hind-brain makes voluntary actions precise and keeps us balanced.

items.question: Which two organs make up the central nervous system?
options: The brain and the spinal cord
The brain and the sense organs
items.explanation: The brain and spinal cord receive and integrate information; the nerves leaving them form the peripheral system.

items.question: Light falls on a shoot from one side. Why does the shoot bend towards the light?
options: Auxin collects on the lit side and stops growth there
Cells on the lit side lose all their water
Auxin moves to the shady side and makes the cells there grow longer
Abscisic acid makes the shady side shrink
items.explanation: Faster growth on the shaded side curves the shoot towards the light.

items.question: What happens when an electrical impulse reaches the end of an axon?
options: The electricity jumps straight into the next neuron
Hormones are released into the blood
Chemicals are released that cross the gap and start an impulse in the next cell
items.explanation: The electrical signal is turned into a chemical one to cross the synapse, then back into an impulse.

items.question: How do muscle cells shorten when a nerve impulse reaches them?
options: Special proteins in them change their shape and arrangement
items.explanation: Muscle proteins rearrange in response to nervous impulses, giving the cell a shorter form.

items.question: When the blood sugar level rises, how does the pancreas respond?
items.explanation: Pancreas cells detect the rise and make more insulin, which brings the level back down.

items.question: Why does a reflex arc give a faster response than thinking about the situation first?
options: Reflexes use hormones, which travel faster than nerve impulses
The brain thinks faster during a reflex
The input nerve is linked to the output nerve in the spinal cord, without waiting for the thinking brain
Muscles move without any nerve signal
items.explanation: Thinking needs many neurons in the brain and takes time; a direct spinal link lets the muscle respond at once.

items.question: Which part of the brain receives sensory impulses, interprets them with stored information and decides how to respond?
items.explanation: The fore-brain is the main thinking part: it has sensory and association areas and passes decisions to motor areas.

items.question: How is the folding of a touch-me-not plant's leaves different from a shoot bending towards light?
options: Leaf folding involves no growth, while bending towards light is caused by growth
Leaf folding is caused by growth, but bending is not
Neither involves any change in the plant's cells
items.explanation: The sensitive plant moves quickly without growing; directional movement of a seedling happens only by growth.

items.question: Which plant hormone is found in high amounts in fruits and seeds, and why?
options: Abscisic acid, because it stops growth there
Cytokinins, because they promote cell division, which is rapid there
Auxin, because it bends fruits towards light
items.explanation: Cytokinins drive cell division, so they are concentrated where cells divide quickly.

items.question: Why is iodised salt recommended in our diet?
options: Iodine is needed to make insulin
Iodine helps the adrenal glands make adrenaline
The thyroid gland needs iodine to make thyroxin
items.explanation: Without enough iodine the thyroid cannot make thyroxin, and goitre may develop.
